selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline state before rotation config (log file, logrotate binary, no prior config)
selected_evidence.summary: Confirmed app.log exists, logrotate installed, logrotate.timer enabled/active, and no pre-existing logrotate rule for inventory app.

selected_evidence.requirement: Logrotate config created (daily, rotate 7, compression, copytruncate)
selected_evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app with the required daily/rotate 7/compress/delaycompress/copytruncate settings and displayed the installed file.
logrotate -d dry run parsed the config without errors and correctly evaluated the rotation schedule.

selected_evidence.requirement: Rotation actually occurs and retains compressed history (7 rotations) while app keeps writing after rotation (copytruncate)
selected_evidence.summary: First forced rotation: copytruncate truncated app.log to 0 bytes and preserved prior content in app.log.1. After truncation, new content was appended to app.log and a second forced rotation moved it to app.log.1 while the earlier app.log.1 was compressed to app.log.2.gz per delaycompress, proving both the rotate/retain/compress pipeline and uninterrupted app writes post-rotation.

selected_evidence.requirement: Cleanup / final steady state of app.log and config
selected_evidence.summary: Removed test rotation artifacts, restored app.log to original baseline content, and reconfirmed the logrotate config file remains in place.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (98aa35f5-6905-42fd-9f07-0e28f75b4fa6), uptime start, and logrotate.timer active/enabled status prior to reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Issued systemctl reboot via a backgrounded delayed shell; the exec call returned 'reboot scheduled' successfully before the node disconnected.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: node unreachable during reboot, then changed boot identity confirmed
selected_evidence.summary: Polling showed connection timeouts/resets while node1 was rebooting, then a successful exec returned a new boot_id (f168820a-9f12-4e23-a26f-d37f5cc6f1a1) and new uptime start (08:21:46), proving an actual restart rather than mere service recovery.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 restart protocol: post-restart recovery of required services/config/data
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, confirmed /etc/logrotate.d/inventory-app persisted intact, app.log data intact, logrotate.timer active and enabled, and logrotate -d still validates the rule correctly.
